```{r data generation, echo = FALSE, results = "hide"}
library(mosaic)
```

Question
========

Welche Parameter hat diese Normalverteilung?

```{r, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="", fig.width=4.5, out.width="50%"}
gf_dist("norm", mean=10, sd=2)
```



Answerlist
----------
* $\mu=10$, $\sigma=10$.
* $\mu=2$, $\sigma=2$.
* $\mu=10$, $\sigma=2$.
* $\mu=2$, $\sigma=10$.


Solution
========

Bei einer Normalverteilung ist der Erwartungswert $\mu$ bei dem Maximum des Grafen abzulesen (-$\,$-$\,$-), hier also $\mu=10$.
Die Standardabweichung ist an den Wendepunkten des Grafen abzulesen, $\mu\pm\sigma$ ($\cdots$), hier also $\sigma=2$.

```{r, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="", fig.width=4.5, out.width="50%"}
yval <- dnorm(8, mean = 10, sd = 2)
gf_dist("norm", mean=10, sd=2) |> 
  gf_vline(xintercept = 10, linetype = 2) |> 
  gf_annotate(y = yval, yend = yval, x = 8, xend = 12, geom = "segment", linetype = 3) |> 
  gf_annotate(y = yval, x = 9, label = "σ", vjust = 2, size = 5) |> 
  gf_annotate(y = yval, x = 11, label = "σ", vjust = 2, size = 5) |>
  gf_annotate(y = 0.05, x = 10, label = "μ", hjust = -0.5, size = 5)
# nachfolgender Code gibt Warnhinweise  
#  gf_segment(yval + yval ~ 8 + 12, linetype = 3 ) |> 
#  gf_text(yval ~ 9, label = "σ", vjust = 2, size = 5) |> 
#  gf_text(yval ~ 11, label = "σ", vjust = 2, size = 5) |>
#  gf_text(0.05 ~ 10, label = "μ", hjust = -0.5, size = 5)
# expression funktioniert gar nicht mehr
```


Answerlist
----------
* Falsch
* Falsch
* Richtig
* Falsch
